title: Protocol #02: Bow Drill Friction Fire Method
summary: A primitive pyrotechnology protocol using mechanical friction between dry softwood and a bow drill to generate carbon dust embers exceeding 400°C, followed by concentrated aeration to achieve ignition.

materials.name: Bow & Vine String (BOW & STRING)
materials.desc: Flexible hardwood limb (ash/hazel, 60-70cm) and durable wild kudzu vine cord or paracord

materials.name: Rotational Spindle (SPINDLE)
materials.desc: Straight 2cm dia x 20cm dry cedar or willow shaft. Blunt top, 45-degree tapered bottom.

materials.name: Hearth Board & Tinder Nest (HEARTH & TINDER)
materials.desc: 15-20mm thick hearth board with 45° V-notch, ember collection leaf, and dry tinder nest

steps.title: V-Notch Carving & Spindle Axis Seating
steps.description: Carve a precise 45-degree V-notch from the edge of the hearth board penetrating directly to the axis center. Place a dry ember collector leaf beneath to trap hot carbon dust.
steps.actionNote: > Field Rule: If the notch angle exceeds 60 degrees, thermal dissipation will prevent the dust from reaching the 400°C ignition threshold.

steps.title: 90° Downward Load & High-Speed Reciprocating Sawing
steps.description: Anchor the hearth board firmly with your left foot and apply 12-15kg downward load using the bearing block. Saw the bow horizontally with full-length strokes at 300-400 RPM until dense white smoke bursts.
steps.actionNote: > Field Rule: Do not stop when smoke first appears. Continue 10-15 full-power acceleration strokes to ensure complete carbonization in the notch.

steps.title: Ember Transfusion & Gentle Aeration Ignition
steps.description: Allow the smoking carbon dust to coalesce into a cohesive coal for 30 seconds. Carefully transfer it into the center of a dry tinder nest, cup at a 45-degree elevation, and supply steady, gentle breaths to ignite flame.
steps.actionNote: > Field Rule: Hold the nest at a 45-degree angle slightly above eye level. Rising thermal updrafts double oxygen intake while keeping toxic smoke away from eyes.

fatalMistake.title: Never blow rashly on premature uncoalesced embers
fatalMistake.description: Blowing prematurely on loose carbon dust will scatter the delicate ember particles, extinguishing the core heat immediately.
fatalMistake.consequence: Failure to start a fire in wilderness freezing conditions leads to irreversible hypothermia and death within 72 hours.
